provisional_claims.summary: Shade cloth did not shelter the tile below it: habitat.effective_shade only checked the tile itself plus left, right and above, leaving out (x, y+1). GROWING.md says shade cloth covers its own tile and all adjoining tiles. Added the missing neighbor.
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(34,8,8); set_structure(w,3,3,'shade_cloth'); effective_shade(w, w.index(3,2)) - w.cell(3,2).shade was 0 (expected 15). The tiles left, right and below the cloth get +15 as expected.

provisional_claims.summary: Rain barrels added 6 moisture every day, including clear days. The documentation (GROWING.md, runtime VERSIONS) says they collect water only on rainy days. water_balance now adds the barrel gain only when the day's rain is above zero.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Put a rain_barrel on a tile and call habitat.water_balance(world, i, 50, 50, 0, 3) with rain=0 (a clear day). It returned 53 when it should return 47; the barrel should do nothing without rain.

provisional_claims.summary: Stress rose for plants at exactly 30 vitality. GROWING.md says stress increases only when vitality is below 30. after_day used `<= 30`; changed it to `< 30`.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Set a plant's vitality to 30 with stress 10, then call habitat.after_day(world,0,0). Stress went to 15; it should drop to 7 (recovery).

provisional_claims.summary: The worm census ignored peat. GROWING.md says "moist, rich soil or peat supports worms", but after_day only counted soil tiles. It now counts both soil and peat.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Set every tile to peat with moisture 60 and nutrients 60, then run after_day. visitors['worms'] was 0; it should be (tile count)//4.

provisional_claims.summary: census() averaged living-plant vitality over all selected tiles (including bare ground) instead of over living plants; FIELD_GUIDE says "vitality averages describe living plants". Fixed divisor to len(living). This also corrects daily history vitality (lantern-hollow example history now matches 59.39 etc.).
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=engine.create(34,16,11); analysis.census(w)['averages']['vitality'] was ~19 (sum/len(cells)) vs expected ~59 (sum/len(living)); replaying examples/hollow-actions.json gave history vitality 19.22 vs 59.39 in examples/lantern-hollow.json.

provisional_claims.summary: census() diversity used log2 while FIELD_GUIDE documents Shannon entropy with natural logarithms. Changed math.log2 to math.log.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Garden with 2 species in equal numbers: diversity was 1.0 (log2); expected ln 2 = 0.6931.

provisional_claims.summary: calendar_day returned the wrong season_day: `(day+1)%12+1` puts day 0 at season day 2 and day 10 at season day 12. Changed to `day%12+1`, so day 0 is season day 1 and day 11 is season day 12.
provisional_claims.reproduction: weather.calendar_day(0)['season_day'] returned 2 (expected 1). calendar_day(11) returned 1 (expected 12).

provisional_claims.summary: suitability()/recommendations ignored shade-cloth shelter: used base cell.shade instead of habitat.effective_shade (imported but unused). FIELD_GUIDE: "Planting advice accounts for ... shelter from structures". Now score/reasons/effective_shade use effective shade.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Place shade_cloth at (1,1); analysis.suitability(w,1,1,'glowcap')['effective_shade'] returned base shade (unchanged), expected base+15.

provisional_claims.summary: recommendations(empty_only=False) still skipped occupied tiles; parameter was validated but ignored. Docs: recommendations "normally omit occupied ground". Now occupied tiles are skipped only when empty_only is true.
provisional_claims.reproduction: analysis.recommendations(w,'moss',limit=1200,empty_only=False) returned only empty tiles; now includes occupied plantable tiles.

provisional_claims.summary: The almanac's longest_dry_spell counted runs of drizzle (rainfall == 8) instead of dry days. FIELD_GUIDE.md says it reports consecutive dry days. It now counts days with rainfall == 0.
provisional_claims.reproduction: almanac(create(34),48): longest_dry_spell equalled the longest run of drizzle days, not the longest run of 'clear' days. Compare it with the entries in the 'days' list.

provisional_claims.summary: forecast() omitted the final day when days is not a multiple of every. FIELD_GUIDE: "--days 10 --every 3 samples elapsed days 0, 3, 6, 9 and 10". Final offset is now always sampled.
provisional_claims.reproduction: analysis.forecast(w,10,3)['timeline'] days were [0,3,6,9] relative; expected [0,3,6,9,10].

provisional_claims.summary: weather.next_weather searched from today (start=world.day). FIELD_GUIDE.md says it finds a matching future day. The window now starts at tomorrow (world.day+1).
provisional_claims.reproduction: Pick a garden whose weather_on(seed, world.day) matches the kind. next_weather(world, kind)['day'] returned world.day (today) instead of a later day.

provisional_claims.summary: The calendar showed one plan occurrence too many. `remaining` counts the occurrence on plan['day'] itself, so valid gaps are 0..remaining-1 intervals, but the check used `gap//repeat <= remaining`. A plan from day 5, interval 3, four runs also listed day 17. Changed to `<`.
provisional_claims.reproduction: schedule(w,'p',5,[[0,0]],'water',repeat=3,runs=4), then calendar(w,20). The plan appeared on days 5, 8, 11, 14 and 17; WORKBENCH.md says only 5, 8, 11 and 14.

provisional_claims.summary: Season calendar was offset by one season: engine.season() used (day//12 + 1) % 4 so day 0 was reported as Highsummer instead of Dawn (docs: "Day zero is the first day of Dawn"). Fixed to SEASONS[(day // 12) % 4].
provisional_claims.reproduction: python3 -c "from mosslight.engine import season; print(season(0), season(12))" printed Highsummer Ember; expected Dawn Highsummer. Also examples/first-garden.json journal logs 'Highsummer settles' on day 12; create(34,16,11)+step 24 now reproduces the example exactly.

provisional_claims.summary: search_notes left out notes dated on the end day because it filtered with `start <= day < end`. WORKBENCH.md promises an inclusive date range, and the default end (today) hid today's notes. Now uses `<= end`.
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(1); add_note(w,'hello'); search_notes(w) returned [] on day 0 (expected one note). search_notes(w,start=0,end=0) was also empty.

provisional_claims.summary: Weather almanac used the wrong season's wetness: weather_on() indexed wetness with (day//12+1)%4, so Dawn got Highsummer's dry odds and Highsummer got Ember's etc. Fixed to (day//12)%4 so Highsummer is the driest season as documented; seeded weather now reproduces examples/first-garden.json (storms on days 9-10).
provisional_claims.reproduction: create(34,16,11); step(w,24) and compare to examples/first-garden.json: before fix moisture/cells/journal diverged heavily (weather sequence differed); after fix identical. weather_on(seed, day) for day in 0..11 uses wetness 0.46 (Dawn).

provisional_claims.summary: The tag filter in search_notes matched substrings, so tag 'pond' also returned notes tagged 'ponds' or 'mudpond'. It now requires an exact normalized tag (`tag in n['tags']`).
provisional_claims.reproduction: add_note(w,'a',['ponds']), then search_notes(w,tag='pond') returned the note. Expected [].

provisional_claims.summary: complete_task ignored its `done` argument and always set done=True, so a task could not be reopened. WORKBENCH.md says tasks can be marked complete or reopened. It now stores the given value.
provisional_claims.reproduction: t=add_task(w,'x',3); complete_task(w,t['id']); complete_task(w,t['id'],False). The task still had done == True.

provisional_claims.summary: Daily water sharing read neighbours' already-updated moisture: engine._one_day computed neighbor_mean from world.cells (partially updated this day) instead of the day's starting snapshot, so results depended on scan order (docs: "A day's development represents the whole garden growing together"). Fixed to average the old snapshot neighbours.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create(34,16,11); step 24 days; compare cells to examples/first-garden.json - moisture diverged before fix; identical after. Tiles later in scan order saw post-update neighbours.

provisional_claims.summary: Bare ground never recovered nutrients: engine set empty tiles to clamp(before.nutrients) with no recovery (docs: "Bare ground slowly recovers one nutrient point a day"). Fixed to +1 per day for empty tiles (planted tiles still use upkeep logic and the before-value for hunger check).
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(34,16,11); cell 51 is empty with nutrients 48; step(w,1) left it at 48 (expected 49). Full 24-day run now matches examples/first-garden.json.

provisional_claims.summary: Engine applied the nutrient-starvation comfort penalty (-7) using the already-updated cell.nutrients (which includes the day's +1 bare-ground recovery / mutated value) instead of the plant's starting nutrients (before.nutrients). Plants on exhausted soil (0 nutrients) escaped the penalty. Fixed to test before.nutrients < upkeep; create(34,16,11)+24 days now reproduces examples/first-garden.json exactly.
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=engine.create(34,16,11); step 24 single days; compare with examples/first-garden.json cells: several nutrient-0 plants had vitality 7 points too high (e.g. index 3: 100 vs 93). After fix: 0 differing cells, journal identical.

provisional_claims.summary: The 'overdue' task filter included tasks due today (`due <= world.day`). WORKBENCH.md defines overdue as earlier days only, while 'due' includes today. Changed it to `due < world.day`.
provisional_claims.reproduction: On day 0, add_task(w,'x',0), then task_list(w,'overdue') returned that task. Expected [].

provisional_claims.summary: Strained-plant nutrient return used the previous day's vitality instead of the updated vitality (engine: '2 if before.vitality < 25'). A plant that fell under 25 on a given day did not return nutrients that day. Fixed to use the day's new vitality, reproducing the shipped example save.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create(34,16,11); step 24; cells[51] and [64] (clover dropping 26->22 on day 11) ended with nutrients 33/27 instead of 35/29 in examples/first-garden.json.

provisional_claims.summary: task_list sorted tasks by id rather than due date. WORKBENCH.md says lists put earlier due dates first. It now sorts by (due, id).
provisional_claims.reproduction: add_task(w,'late',9), then add_task(w,'soon',2). task_list(w) returned 'late' before 'soon'.

provisional_claims.summary: Commands incremented revision by more than one: commands.execute set trial.revision = trial.revision+1 after the dispatched tool had already incremented it (and grow incremented per day). A command must advance the revision by exactly one (replay preserves each command's normal revision behavior). Fixed to world.revision + 1.
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(34); execute(w, {"op":"tend","args":{"x":0,"y":0,"action":"water"}}) -> revision 2 instead of 1; replaying examples/hollow-actions.json gave revision 37 vs 16 in examples/lantern-hollow.json.

provisional_claims.summary: press_specimen left vitality out of the specimen record. That broke the save: every later command failed validation with "vitality must be an integer from 0 to 100", and replaying examples/hollow-actions.json crashed. The markdown export also read item['vitality']. Specimens now store the full cell measurements, including vitality.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Run replay(create(34), json.load(open('examples/hollow-actions.json'))). It raised ValueError on the 'specimen' command; the reference output is examples/lantern-hollow.json.

provisional_claims.summary: Scheduled care plans never advanced: run_plans held a reference to the plan dict, but tend_many replaces world.__dict__ (new workbench), so remaining/day/status updates went to a stale copy; plans stayed pending on the same day forever and later runs never happened. Fixed by re-fetching the entry after tend_many.
provisional_claims.reproduction: replay examples/hollow-actions.json on create(34): plan stayed {day:2, remaining:3} and the day-5 pour never ran; expected {day:8, remaining:1} as in examples/lantern-hollow.json.

provisional_claims.summary: Shade cloth did not shelter the tile below it: habitat.effective_shade only checked (x,y),(x-1,y),(x+1,y),(x,y-1), missing (x,y+1), so the tile north of a cloth got no canopy (docs: cloth shelters its own tile and adjoining tiles). Added the missing neighbour.
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(34); set_structure(w,1,1,'shade_cloth'); effective_shade(w, w.index(1,0)) equalled w.cell(1,0).shade (no +15), while (1,2) got +15.

provisional_claims.summary: Plant comfort ignored structures' shade: engine computed comfort from cell.shade (base) instead of effective_shade, so shade cloth had no effect on plant vitality (docs: shelter affects growing conditions without changing base shade). Fixed to use the effective shade.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Replay examples/hollow-actions.json on create(34): cells (2,1) and (1,2) next to the shade cloth had vitality 63/73 vs 68/83 in examples/lantern-hollow.json. After fix, replay matches the example exactly.

provisional_claims.summary: Hush season penalty (-2 comfort) was applied to glowcaps too. GROWING.md: "Hush slows most plants, while glowcaps remain suited to the season." Penalty now skips glowcap.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Create garden, plant glowcap at comfortable tile, advance to day 36 (Hush): glowcap vitality gain per day dropped by 2 compared with Ember under identical conditions. After fix, glowcap comfort unchanged in Hush while moss/fern/clover still get -2.

provisional_claims.summary: Plants died of old age at a hardcoded age >105 regardless of species; the field guide lists species lifespans (glowcap 75). Engine now uses SPECIES_GUIDE[species]["lifespan"], so glowcaps return to the soil after age 75.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Set a glowcap cell age=75 vitality=90 in a comfortable spot, step 1 day: glowcap survived at age 76 (should return to soil since guide lifespan is 75).

provisional_claims.summary: gardening.rectangle dropped the right-hand column because it used range(left, right) for x. Rectangles are inclusive (blueprints use width abs(x2-x1)+1), so the column is now range(left, right+1). Before the fix, blueprint() also produced fewer tiles than width*height, so validate_blueprint rejected it with "Blueprint tile count mismatch".
provisional_claims.reproduction: rectangle(w,0,0,2,1) returned 4 tiles instead of 6. transform_blueprint(blueprint(w,0,0,3,2)) raised "Blueprint tile count mismatch", which breaks the README CLI command `blueprint hollow.json --rect 0 0 3 2 --turns 1`.

provisional_claims.summary: The circle brush used Manhattan distance (dx+dy > radius), which made it identical to the diamond brush. It now keeps tiles with dx²+dy² <= r².
provisional_claims.reproduction: len(brush(w,5,5,2,'circle')) returned 13, the same as the diamond. A circle of radius 2 should include (6,6) and cover 13 tiles vs... e.g. at radius 3 the circle has 29 tiles and the diamond 25.

provisional_claims.summary: transplant reset the moved plant's stress to 0 at the destination. WORKBENCH.md says a transplant carries age and stress with the plant. The destination tile now takes the source tile's stress, and the source (now empty) is reset.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Give a plant at (0,0) stress 40, then transplant(w,0,0,1,0) to an empty tile. The destination stress was 0 (expected 40).

provisional_claims.summary: Save validation accepted empty cells that carried age or vitality as long as not both were nonzero (used `and` instead of `or`). Error text is "Empty cell cannot have age or vitality". Fixed to reject when either is nonzero.
provisional_claims.reproduction: d=create().to_dict(); pick an empty cell and set age=5, vitality=0; World.from_dict(d) was accepted. Now raises ValueError.

provisional_claims.summary: prune had no bounds: age could go negative and vitality could pass 100. The next command's save validation then failed ("Cell value outside valid range"). Pruning now clamps age at 0 and vitality at 100.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Plant moss (age 0), then execute(w,{'op':'prune','args':{'x':0,'y':0}}). It raised ValueError because the age became -5. A plant at vitality 96 also ended above 100.

provisional_claims.summary: World.to_dict() returned a shallow copy of the journal (list of the same dict objects), so editing the returned save mutated the live garden's journal. PORTABILITY: to_dict "returns an independently editable save representation". Now deep-copies the journal.
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(); d=w.to_dict(); d['journal'][0]['text']='x'; w.journal[0]['text'] became 'x'. After fix original stays unchanged.

provisional_claims.summary: craft checked inventory against the cost of one batch rather than cost*amount. It then subtracted cost*amount, which drove balances negative (for example fiber -3). The check now compares against cost*amount.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Set inventory fiber=3, then craft(w,'compost',2). It succeeded with fiber=-3; it should raise 'Need 6 fiber' and leave the inventory unchanged.

provisional_claims.summary: Workbench save validation only rejected plants on ponds, although stones are also unplantable (error message "Ponds and stones cannot contain plants"). Now rejects plants on stone tiles too.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Save with workbench tile terrain 'stone' on a cell with species 'moss' loaded without error; now raises ValueError.

provisional_claims.summary: nursery.water_batch added one day of hydration. WORKBENCH.md says watering restores a full three-day supply. It now sets hydration to 3.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Start a seed batch, advance 3 days so hydration reaches 0, then water_batch. Hydration was 1 (expected 3).

provisional_claims.summary: Dry days still advanced a nursery batch's development age. WORKBENCH.md says dry days halt development and weaken the batch. advance_nursery no longer increments age when hydration is 0; it only applies the vitality loss.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Start a glowcap batch and set hydration=0. advance_nursery(w) raised age from 0 to 1 even though the batch was dry; the age should stay 0 while vitality drops by 20.

provisional_claims.summary: Workbench identifier validation: ids equal to next_id were accepted (check used > instead of >=; next_id is the next id to be allocated, message says "below next_id"), and uniqueness was only checked per collection even though ids come from one shared counter, so a loaded save could later allocate a duplicate id. Now ids must be < next_id and unique across notes/specimens/tasks/beds/plans/rules/nursery.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Save with next_id=2 and a note id 2 loaded; subsequent add_task allocated id 2 again (duplicate). Also a note id 1 and a task id 1 were both accepted. Both now rejected.

provisional_claims.summary: plant_out took 4 nutrients only for the batch's last seedling. WORKBENCH.md says each planted seedling uses four nutrient points from its new site. It now always subtracts 4 (floored at 0).
provisional_claims.reproduction: Plant the first seedling from a ready batch with count 3 into a tile with 50 nutrients. The tile kept 50 (expected 46).

provisional_claims.summary: schedule() rejected tomorrow as a plan start day (minimum was world.day+2). Docs: "Plans require a future first day" / "A care plan begins on a future day". Minimum is now world.day+1.
provisional_claims.reproduction: On day 0: execute(w,{"op":"schedule","args":{"name":"p","day":1,"tiles":[[0,0]],"action":"water"}}) raised "Scheduled day must be an integer from 2..."; now accepted.

provisional_claims.summary: Blueprint horizontal mirror produced out-of-range coordinates: transform_blueprint set x = width - x (x=0 became width, outside 0..width-1, and validation later rejects it / tiles shift). Fixed to width-1-x.
provisional_claims.reproduction: b=blueprint(create(34),0,0,2,1); transform_blueprint(b,0,True) gave x values 1..3 for a width-3 pattern (x=3 invalid); now 0..2 with the moss at (2,1) mirrored to (0,1).

provisional_claims.summary: add_bed() compared bed names case-sensitively, allowing "Moss corner" and "moss corner" — but save validation requires case-insensitively unique bed names, so the resulting garden could no longer be validated/saved (command fails at re-validation or save becomes unloadable). Duplicate check now uses casefold.
provisional_claims.reproduction: planning.add_bed(w,'Moss',[[0,0]]); planning.add_bed(w,'moss',[[1,0]]) succeeded; World.from_dict(w.to_dict()) then raised "Bed names must be unique". Now second add_bed raises "A bed with that name already exists".

provisional_claims.summary: Blueprint clockwise quarter turn was off by one: transform_blueprint rotated with new_x = height - y, yielding x values 1..height (out of range) instead of 0..height-1. Fixed to height-1-y.
provisional_claims.reproduction: transform_blueprint(blueprint(create(34),0,0,2,1),1) produced tiles with x=2 for a width-2 result (and CLI blueprint --turns 1 yields an invalid pattern rejected by validate_blueprint/apply). Now coordinates are 0..1 x 0..2.

provisional_claims.summary: execute() accepted commands with arbitrary extra top-level keys (check was only that "op" is present) despite the error "Command accepts only op and args" and docs "A JSON command uses op and args". Now requires op and rejects keys other than op/args.
provisional_claims.reproduction: execute(w,{"op":"grow","args":{"days":1},"extra":1}) succeeded; now raises ValueError("Command accepts only op and args").

provisional_claims.summary: Care plans could not start tomorrow: planning.schedule required day >= world.day+2, but docs require only a future first day (world.day+1). Fixed minimum to world.day+1.
provisional_claims.reproduction: schedule(create(34),'a',1,[[0,0]],'water') on day 0 raised 'Scheduled day must be an integer from 2...'; now accepted.

provisional_claims.summary: Bed names were only unique case-sensitively in add_bed, while save validation casefolds bed names; adding 'Bed' then 'bed' succeeded and produced a garden that failed to re-validate (command then errors / save unloadable). Fixed add_bed to compare casefolded names.
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(34); add_bed(w,'Bed',[[0,0]]); add_bed(w,'bed',[[0,0]]) succeeded, then World.from_dict(w.to_dict()) raised 'Bed names must be unique'. Now the second add is rejected.

provisional_claims.summary: experiment() re-ran every treatment event on every later offset (`event['offset'] <= offset`), so a single offset-0 watering happened again before each day. FIELD_GUIDE.md says events apply at their offset. The condition is now `==`.
provisional_claims.reproduction: experiment(create(34,8,6),5,[{'name':'wet','events':[{'offset':0,'command':{'op':'tend','args':{'x':0,'y':0,'action':'water'}}}]}]). The treatment's journal/revision showed 6 pours instead of 1.

provisional_claims.summary: Experiment branches left out the final observation when `days` was not a multiple of `every`. FIELD_GUIDE.md says initial and final observations are always included. The sampling condition is now `offset%every == 0 or offset == days`.
provisional_claims.reproduction: experiment(w,5,[{'name':'t','events':[]}],2) sampled offsets [0,2,4]. Expected [0,2,4,5].

provisional_claims.summary: import_csv advanced the revision twice (revision = old+1 then += 1). Fixed to a single increment.
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(34); r=w.revision; import_csv(w, export_csv(w)); w.revision-r was 2, now 1.

provisional_claims.summary: Experiment against_control deltas had the wrong sign. compare(trial, control) computed control minus treatment, but the deltas are documented as differences from control. The call is now compare(control, trial), so population_delta and coverage_delta mean treatment minus control.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Run a treatment that plants moss at an empty tile at offset 0 with days=1. against_control.population_delta.moss came out negative (-1); expected +1.

provisional_claims.summary: CLI errors exited with status 1 but PORTABILITY.md documents "CLI errors go to stderr with exit code 2". Fixed __main__ error path to return 2.
provisional_claims.reproduction: python3 -B -m mosslight inspect missing.json; echo $? -> 1 before, 2 after.

provisional_claims.summary: Treatment names were compared case-sensitively against a set of casefolded names. That let 'Control' or 'Wet'/'wet' through even though control is reserved and names must be unique. The check now uses name.casefold().
provisional_claims.reproduction: experiment(w,2,[{'name':'Control','events':[]}]) was accepted; expected ValueError('Treatment names must be unique; control is reserved'). The same happened with [{'name':'Wet'},{'name':'wet'}].

provisional_claims.summary: The shade map drew the ground's base shade. FIELD_GUIDE.md says shade maps show the shelter plants experience, including structures. render_map now uses habitat.effective_shade for layer 'shade'; it was already imported but never used.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Place a shade_cloth at (1,1) and call render_map(w,'shade'). The tile (1,1) label/title still showed the base cell.shade instead of shade+15.

provisional_claims.summary: render_history spaced points by list index. It computed x from h['day'] relative to first=0 and last=len(history)-1, so any history not starting at day 0, or with gaps, was misplaced or drawn off the plot, and the axis labels were wrong. FIELD_GUIDE/DESIGN say charts place observations at their actual dates. first and last now come from the first and last history days.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Set history to two points on days 100 and 110, then render_history(w). The circles landed at x far beyond the 720px plot and the labels read 'Day 0'/'Day 1'; expected x=60 and x=720, labelled Day 100/Day 110.

provisional_claims.summary: render_svg added tabindex="0" role="button" to every tile even for standalone (non-interactive) artwork exports, making static SVG exports claim to be interactive buttons; only interactive studio SVGs should be focusable (render_map already does this). Now attributes are only emitted when interactive=True; rendering examples/first-garden.json and lantern-hollow.json now matches the shipped example SVGs byte-for-byte (except trailing newline).
provisional_claims.reproduction: render.render_svg(model.load('examples/first-garden.json')) contained '<g class="tile" data-x="0" data-y="0" tabindex="0" role="button">' while examples/first-garden.svg has no tabindex for standalone art.

provisional_claims.summary: Courier causal dominance test was inverted: courier.precedes(a,b) iterated b.keys(), so an event whose writer was absent from another event's context was treated as superseded. Concurrent edits vanished from observations (fields came back empty). Fixed to iterate a.keys().
provisional_claims.reproduction: a=new_packet('desk'); put(a,'r',{'text':'Fern'}); b=merge(new_packet('field'),a); b['peer']='field'; b['counter']=0; put(b,'r',{'text':'fern'}); put(a,'r',{'text':'FERN'}); observations(merge(a,b)) -> fields {'text': []}. Now both concurrent values are kept as a conflict.

provisional_claims.summary: GardenServer.publish had three bugs when autosaving with --file. (1) It set self.world = trial before saving, so the undo stack recorded the new garden instead of the previous one, and a failed save left the unsaved garden live despite the documented "500 with the previous garden preserved". (2) It trimmed the undo stack with [:30], keeping the oldest 30 edits instead of the last 30. (3) It kept stale redo entries after a new edit. publish now saves first, pushes the previous garden, keeps the last 30 undo states, clears redo, and only then swaps in the trial.
provisional_claims.reproduction: make_server(create(34,8,6),0,path), POST /api/command to water (0,0), then POST /api/undo. Moisture stayed at the watered value because the undo entry was the new garden. After 31 edits, undo also reverted the oldest states.

provisional_claims.summary: The server's revision check only rejected revisions lower than the current one. It accepted revisions from the future and bools (isinstance(True,int)). DESIGN.md says a stale or noninteger revision returns 409. It now rejects anything that is not an exact int equal to the current revision.
provisional_claims.reproduction: POST /api/command with revision 999 on a revision-0 garden returned 200; expected 409. The same happened with 'revision': true.

provisional_claims.summary: Courier observations collapsed concurrent values that differ only by case: distinct values were keyed by json.dumps(...).casefold(), so 'FERN' vs 'fern' conflict showed a single value (docs: text retains its exact spelling and case; concurrent different values remain available). Removed casefold.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Two writers concurrently put text 'FERN' and 'fern' for the same record; observations(merge(a,b)) reported one value and conflicted False. Now ['FERN','fern'], conflicted True.

provisional_claims.summary: POST /api/import always overwrote the imported save's revision whenever a world was supplied (condition tested "world" in body instead of "revision" in body). PORTABILITY: "Legacy imports without a revision remain supported and retain the imported save's revision." Now the revision is advanced only for revision-checked imports.
provisional_claims.reproduction: POST /api/import {"world": <save with revision 50>} (no revision) → response world.revision was server revision+1; expected 50. With {"world":..., "revision": current} the revision is still current+1.

provisional_claims.summary: Courier: concurrent edit + deletion hid the observation. observations() skipped a record if any $alive head was False; docs say a simultaneous edit and deletion keeps the observation visible until reviewed. Now a record is hidden only when all alive heads are False.
provisional_claims.reproduction: a=new_packet('desk'); put(a,'r',{'text':'x'}); b=copy.deepcopy(a); b['peer']='field'; b['counter']=0; remove(b,'r'); put(a,'r',{'text':'y'}); observations(merge(a,b)) returned [] ; now shows record r with text 'y'.

provisional_claims.summary: Undo and redo set the revision to the restored snapshot's revision + 1, which moves the revision backwards (5 → 3+1 = 4). A tab holding an older revision could then write over newer work. The server now sets current revision + 1 so revisions only increase.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Make two edits (revision reaches 2 through commands), then POST /api/undo. The world revision dropped to 2 instead of rising to 3; a stale client that read revision 2 could then write.

provisional_claims.summary: courier.acknowledged used max across peers, reporting progress seen by any device; docs say it reports progress seen by every named device and a missing acknowledgement supplies no progress. Fixed to min (missing peer counts as 0).
provisional_claims.reproduction: acknowledged({'a':{'w':3},'b':{'w':1}},['a','b','c']) returned {'w':3}; expected {'w':0} (c has not acknowledged; with ['a','b'] expected 1).

provisional_claims.summary: Courier merge treated coverage globally: _covered() took the max over every record's context, so knowledge about one observation made the merge drop another observation's events (docs: sharing one observation doesn't imply the recipient saw other observations' edits/deletions). Fixed to use only the event's own record context.
provisional_claims.reproduction: a=new_packet('desk'); put(a,'r1',{'text':'one'}); put(a,'r2',{'text':'two'}); f=copy.deepcopy(a); p=project(checkpoint(a),['r1']); observations(merge(f,p)) lost r2 entirely. After fix (together with project fix) r1 and r2 both remain.

provisional_claims.summary: courier.project kept causal contexts for records it did not select, so merging a selection into a complete notebook deleted the unselected observations (their events looked superseded). project now keeps only contexts of the requested records.
provisional_claims.reproduction: a=new_packet('desk'); put(a,'r1',{'text':'one'}); put(a,'r2',{'text':'two'}); p=project(checkpoint(a),['r1']); observations(merge(copy.deepcopy(a),p)) returned only r1; docs: merging a selection preserves observations it did not include. Now r2 is preserved.

provisional_claims.summary: Courier merge accepted conflicting reuse of a writer event identity when only the field/value differed: merge compared only event['record']. Two packets with the same (peer,counter) but different field/value merged silently (left copy won). Now any differing event content under the same dot is rejected.
provisional_claims.reproduction: a=new_packet('desk'); put(a,'r',{'tags':['fern']}); b=new_packet('desk'); put(b,'r',{'tags':['moss']}); merge(a,b) succeeded; now raises 'A writer sequence was reused with different content'.

provisional_claims.summary: courier.put stored caller-owned field values by reference, so mutating a list/dict after put changed the packet's recorded observation (docs: supplied field values remain owned by the caller). _emit now deep-copies the value.
provisional_claims.reproduction: a=new_packet('desk'); tags=['fern']; put(a,'r',{'tags':tags}); tags.append('x'); observations(a) showed ['fern','x']; now ['fern'].

provisional_claims.summary: History replay reused checkpoints keyed only by the root and the LAST event of the prefix (events[-1:]), so any two histories that end with the same event (e.g. after a correction/removal of an earlier event, or cherry-picked/rebased shared events) got a stale cached garden from a different prefix. Checkpoint key now digests the full event prefix.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create history; append note A (e1), note B (e2), tend water (e3). correct(branch,{e1:null}) replays [e2,e3]; the cache lookup for prefix [e2,e3] matched the key of [e1,e2,e3] (same last event) and returned the old garden still containing note A. verify() on the corrected branch reports matches=False. After fix the corrected branch has only note B.

provisional_claims.summary: History replay resolved object references using the local ID recorded when the event was authored (event.bindings) instead of the logical entity's current local ID. After a correction removed an earlier object, later edit/complete/delete events targeted the wrong object or failed ("No notes entry"), contradicting HISTORY.md ("References in later actions continue to identify the objects their authors selected, even when a revised history assigns different local numbers"). _resolved_command now uses the resolved entity id.
provisional_claims.reproduction: append note A (id1), note B (id2), edit_note ident=2 "B2"; correct({A_event:null}) -> B now has id 1 but edit replayed with ident 2 → conflict/edit wrong note. After fix corrected branch is ready with notes [(1,'B2')].

provisional_claims.summary: cherry_pick identified "shared" actions by a digest of the command content, so an independently authored but identical action (e.g. the same watering on two forks) was treated as already present and raised a concurrent-edit conflict (or was silently dropped). HISTORY.md: "A shared action is included once; independently authored actions remain distinct." Pick identity is now the event id.
provisional_claims.reproduction: fork F and G from same branch; append {"op":"tend","args":{"x":0,"y":0,"action":"water"}} to each; cherry_pick(F, G, [F's water event]) raised HistoryConflict "An already present event has different content". After fix the picked event is appended (5 -> 6 events).

provisional_claims.summary: A merged courier packet could not safely continue the left writer's work: merge kept left['counter'] even when the right packet contained newer events by the same writer, so the next put reused an existing (peer,counter) identity and later merges failed with 'writer sequence reused'. merge now advances counter to the merged clock for the left writer.
provisional_claims.reproduction: old=new_packet('desk'); put(old,'r',{'text':'a'}); new=copy.deepcopy(old); put(new,'r',{'text':'b'}); m=merge(old,new); put(m,'r',{'text':'c'}); merge(m,new) raised ValueError. Now works and shows 'c'.

provisional_claims.summary: HistoryStore.correct canonicalized numeric IDs in replacement commands against the branch's FINAL garden rather than the garden at the corrected event's position (the loop's index was unused). Replacements referencing objects that existed at that point but were later deleted were rejected, and IDs could bind to later objects. HISTORY.md: "Numeric IDs in a replacement refer to the garden at that point in the history." Now replays the original prefix before the event for canonicalization.
provisional_claims.reproduction: append note A (id1), task T, delete_entry notes 1. correct({T_event: {"op":"edit_note","args":{"ident":1,"content":"A!"}}}) raised "No live object has that local ID" (A deleted in final garden). After fix the correction is accepted and branch is ready.

provisional_claims.summary: HistoryStore.rebase used the parent branch's CURRENT head as the merge base instead of the fork's recorded base_revision. Any parent actions appended after the fork looked like deletions by the child, so rebasing silently dropped the updated parent's new work (and recorded the wrong base in the origin). Now uses source["base_revision"].
provisional_claims.reproduction: P: append note e1; C=fork(P); append note c1 to C; append note p1 to P; rebase(C,P) produced notes ['e1','c1'] (p1 lost). After fix: ['e1','p1','c1'] and origin.base_revision is the fork point.

provisional_claims.summary: Raw-save merge conflated independently created records: save_merge._logical_id mapped every identifier to ["base", id], so notes/tasks created on both replicas with the same new id collided (reported as a conflict or one silently replaced the other). New records are now keyed by their replica origin and receive fresh unique ids; inherited ids keep their identity.
provisional_claims.reproduction: b=create(34); add_note(b,'base'); l,r = copies; add_note(l,'left note'); add_note(r,'right note'); reconcile(b,l,r,left_origin='desk',right_origin='field') returned a conflict on /records/notes/["base",2]. Now 'ready' with notes 1,3,4 and next_id 5.

provisional_claims.summary: Rebase ordering check (_respect_shared_order) only enforced the target branch's order of shared events and ignored the local branch's authored order (the local argument was unused), so incompatible action orders were silently resolved in favour of the target instead of raising an order-conflict for review. HISTORY.md: "Conflicting changes or incompatible action orders require review". Both local and target sequences now constrain the order.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Construct local history with shared events [a,b] and target with [b,a] (e.g. via cherry-pick in different orders) and rebase: previously returned target order without conflict; now raises HistoryConflict kind "order-conflict".

provisional_claims.summary: Courier events took their causal context from the whole packet clock (`dict(packet['clock'])`). After a recipient merged a projection of observation X, its clock covered the sender's edits to other observations it had never received. A later local edit to observation Y then silently superseded the sender's concurrent Y edit, contrary to COURIER.md ("Sharing one observation does not imply that the recipient has seen another observation's edits or deletions"). _emit now uses the observation's own coverage, record_clock(packet, record).
provisional_claims.reproduction: full=new_packet('f'); put(full,'x',{'text':'x0'}); put(full,'y',{'text':'y0'}); g=merge(new_packet('g'),full); put(g,'x',{'text':'x1'}); put(g,'y',{'text':'y-g'}); m=merge(full,project(g,['x'])); put(m,'y',{'text':'y-f'}); observations(merge(m,g)) showed y text ['y-f'] only. Expected a conflict ['y-f','y-g'].

provisional_claims.summary: courier.checkpoint set every record's context to the packet's whole clock. After merging a partial projection, compacting therefore claimed coverage of other records' events that were never received, and a later merge with the full sender packet dropped those unseen concurrent edits as "covered". checkpoint now records each observation's own coverage (record_clock).
provisional_claims.reproduction: Same setup as the projection case: m=merge(full, project(g,['x'])); put(m,'y',{'text':'y-f'}); observations(merge(checkpoint(m), g)) lost g's concurrent 'y-g' value. Expected ['y-f','y-g'] conflicted. COURIER.md: compacting preserves meaning when it meets partial copies.

provisional_claims.summary: courier.merge kept the left packet's counter even when the right packet held later events from the same writer, for example a newer copy of that device's own packet. Continuing the merged packet ("A merged packet keeps the left writer and can be used to continue that writer's work") then reused event identities that already existed, and later merges were rejected as conflicting reuse. The merged counter is now max(left counter, merged clock[left peer]).
provisional_claims.reproduction: d1=new_packet('d'); put(d1,'r',{'text':'1'}); d2=copy.deepcopy(d1); put(d2,'r',{'text':'2'}); mm=merge(d1,d2); put(mm,'r',{'text':'3'}); merge(mm,d2) raised 'A writer sequence was reused with different content' because mm reused dots d:3/d:4.

provisional_claims.summary: History exchange reconciliation truncated the set of maximal common ancestors to a single (lexicographically first) publication (`return maximal[:1]`). In criss-cross collaboration (both collaborators previously reconciled the same work), merges used an arbitrary partial base, so shared work could be treated as new/removed and later edits or reversions lost or spuriously conflicted. The recursive comparison() already combines multiple bases; _common_bases now returns all maximal common ancestors.
provisional_claims.reproduction: announce G; checkouts A,B add notes a/b and publish A1,B1; both reconcile A1,B1 (M1,M2); A edits a on M1 → A2; B edits N on M2 → B2; reconcile(A2,B2): common maximal ancestors are {A1,B1} but only one was used as base. After fix the base is the merge of both and the result keeps N2, a2 and b.

provisional_claims.summary: Upgrading a format-1 workspace catalog rebuilt the label index with the old casefold-only key function and installed the format-2 NFKC/whitespace normalizer only afterwards. The index then disagreed with catalog_key: searches returned nothing and PRAGMA integrity_check reported "row N missing from index catalog_by_label". _upgrade_keys now installs the new key function before REINDEX.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Create a v1 catalog (catalog_format version 1, index built with the casefold key) holding labels 'Field  Pond' and 'ＦＩＥＬＤ pond', then open it with WorkspaceCatalog(path). search('field pond') returned [] (expected both), and integrity_check listed the rows as missing from the index.

provisional_claims.summary: field_calibration.estimate computed the least-squares slope from raw sums (Σt² − (Σt)²/n and Σty − ΣtΣy/n). That cancels catastrophically for realistic epoch timestamps with fractional seconds, so the estimates were wrong. The slope now uses centered offsets, the same centering already used for the intercept.
provisional_claims.reproduction: b=1.7e9+0.25; estimate([{'timestamp':b,'moisture':42},{'timestamp':b+60,'moisture':44},{'timestamp':b+120,'moisture':43}], b+120) returned 43.50223. The same readings at timestamps 0/60/120 give exactly 43.5, and a time shift must not change the fit. Negative timestamps (-b...) were affected the same way.

provisional_claims.summary: Campaigns ignored their recorded ecological release: runtime.execution_version() always returned CURRENT_VERSION ('conservation-2'), so a campaign created with --version classic-1 executed under conservation-2 rain-barrel rules (and replay/report differed from ordinary experiments). It now returns definition['runtime']['id'].
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(34); put rain_barrel on row 3; cid=CampaignStore(db).create(w,12,treatments,3,'classic-1'); run work_once to completion; result(cid) != experiment(w,12,treatments,3) before fix (barrel tiles drier), equal after.

provisional_claims.summary: Campaign publish accepted results from stale/foreign workers: the UPDATE guard was '(generation = ? OR owner != ?)', so a worker whose lease was reclaimed (or any mismatched owner) could overwrite branch progress. Guard is now 'generation = ? AND owner = ?' so only the current lease holder publishes.
provisional_claims.reproduction: c1=store.claim(cid, lease_seconds=1); advance clock past lease; c2=store.claim(cid); store.publish(c1, store.compute(c1)) returned True (stale worker accepted, then c2 publishes again → duplicated/skipped offsets). Now returns False.

provisional_claims.summary: Campaign publish committed branch progress and its checkpoint/report in separate transactions (COMMIT then BEGIN IMMEDIATE between the state UPDATE and the checkpoint insert), so an interruption or concurrent worker could leave progress without its checkpoint or a completed campaign without its archived report. Now one transaction.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Inspect CampaignStore.publish: after 'accepted' it executed COMMIT and a new BEGIN IMMEDIATE before _checkpoint/_archive_report; failure in _checkpoint (e.g. duplicate offset from a raced worker) rolled back only the checkpoint while branch state stayed advanced.

provisional_claims.summary: Campaign compaction deleted checkpoints that existing forks descend from: compact() computed the 'protected' lineage set but never used it, so provenance(child) later failed with 'Checkpoint is unavailable'. Protected (ordinal, offset) pairs are now kept.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Complete a 12-day campaign, child=store.fork(cid,2,4); store.compact(cid,5) removed checkpoint (2,4); store.provenance(child) raised ValueError. Now the checkpoint survives and provenance works.

provisional_claims.summary: Campaign fork re-applied care already performed at the checkpoint: fork kept parent events with offset >= checkpoint offset, so an event at the fork offset (already in the checkpoint garden) ran again at offset 0 of the child. Docs: care already performed at the checkpoint remains part of its starting garden. Now only events strictly after the checkpoint carry over.
provisional_claims.reproduction: treatments.json 'Extra water' has events at offsets 1 and 4; after completing, fork(cid, 2, 4) produced child treatment events [{offset:0, water}] (double watering). Now child events are [].

provisional_claims.summary: irrigation_flow.allocate never followed residual (reverse) arcs because route() skipped every arc whose pipe was None. The augmenting-path search was therefore a greedy first-fit, not a maximum flow, and it under-delivered even though IRRIGATION.md says the system delivers as much water as the outlets, supply and pipe capacities permit. Residual arcs are now traversable, so the search finds a true max flow.
provisional_claims.reproduction: allocate([{'from':'s','to':'a','capacity':1},{'from':'s','to':'b','capacity':1},{'from':'a','to':'o1','capacity':1},{'from':'a','to':'o2','capacity':1},{'from':'b','to':'o1','capacity':1}],'s',{'o1':1,'o2':1},5) returned total 1. The achievable maximum is 2 (s→a→o2, s→b→o1).

provisional_claims.summary: Staged studies: later stages started every promoted treatment (and control) from the previous stage's CONTROL checkpoint, discarding the treatment's earlier care and results. STUDIES.md: "Later stages continue the promoted treatments ... They extend the same experiments, preserving earlier care and results." _start_stage now continues each treatment from its own completed checkpoint.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create study from examples/study.json and work to completion; report(stage=1).outcomes[*].parent.treatment was 'control' for Water/Compost jobs and their worlds lacked stage-0 care. After fix each job's parent is its own treatment checkpoint.

provisional_claims.summary: Staged studies finalized a stage decision as soon as ONE garden had a complete control and all treatments (checked support["common"] instead of support["terminal"]). Decisions depended on worker completion order, other gardens' results were excluded while still pending, and a stage where no garden became eligible never recorded the documented failed decision (study hung "running"). Now the decision is made only when all stage trials are complete or failed.
provisional_claims.reproduction: examples/study.json with 2 sources: work jobs so that source 'north' finishes control+all treatments first → stage 0 report was saved immediately with cohort common=['north'] and 'south' excluded though still pending; next stage dispatched with only north. Also force a treatment failure on every source → study never became 'failed'. After fix report waits for all jobs and failed decision is recorded.

provisional_claims.summary: The irrigation solver merged search states by their aggregate census (population and rounded averages) instead of the full garden. Schedules that watered different tiles with the same totals were treated as identical and one was thrown away, although their futures differ. solve() could then return a schedule worse than the optimum, contrary to IRRIGATION.md ("highest total garden vitality ... including the effects of watering on later days"). States are now identified by world + offset + remaining.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create(14,4,4) with two outlets n=[[0,0],[1,0]] and s=[[0,3],[1,3]] (demand 30, pipe capacity 30 each), choices north/south, 3 days, supply 60. solve() scored 319, but brute force over replay() of all 8 schedules finds 321.

provisional_claims.summary: Ensemble report(revision) did not return the published report: it replaced the archived envelope's result with a summary of the current node outcomes, so a revision-0 report changed after later edits (docs: each published report belongs to one input revision and remains available after later edits). report() now returns the stored envelope unchanged.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create examples/ensemble.json, work to completion, r0=report(eid); edit plan:water; work; report(eid,0) != r0 (shows revision-1 outcomes). After fix equal, and replay(eid,0)==r0['result'].

provisional_claims.summary: Ensemble cache reuse mislabeled comparison members: evaluate() took the trial identity from the cached origin, so two sources with equal saves both reported the first source's replicate label (south bed outcomes labeled 'north bed'), breaking pairing. Identity now always comes from the requested node; cache origin is kept as provenance.
provisional_claims.reproduction: examples/ensemble.json with sources['south bed'] = copy of 'north bed'; after work, report outcomes identities were north/north/north/north; docs say source labels identify distinct members even for equal saves. Now north,north,south,south.

provisional_claims.summary: Ensemble summaries paired treatments with the wrong controls: summarize() zipped controls.values() (all complete controls in insertion order) with the treatment rows of paired replicates, so when any replicate was excluded (failed trial) the remaining pairs were misaligned. Now pairs are built per replicate label.
provisional_claims.reproduction: summarize(definition, outcomes) where replicate A's treatment failed but B's succeeded: paired_ids=['B'] but pair used control A with treatment B, giving wrong mean_delta. Now control B is paired with treatment B.

provisional_claims.summary: Ensemble publish accepted results computed from superseded inputs: validation checked only the node's previously known reads (empty for a never-computed node), so an edit made between prepare and publish went undetected and a stale outcome was stored for the new revision. publish now validates the digests of the inputs actually read by the computation.
provisional_claims.reproduction: eid=create(example); t=prepare(eid); edit(eid,{'source:north bed': modified}); publish(t, compute(t)) returned True and the revision-1 report used the old source. Now returns False and the node is recomputed; replay(eid)==report(eid)['result'].

provisional_claims.summary: field_calibration.estimate did not average readings that share a timestamp: duplicate-timestamp readings were fed individually into the least-squares fit, over-weighting that instant (docs: when observations share a timestamp, their average is used). Readings are now grouped per timestamp and averaged before the trend fit.

Conditional care rules were evaluated against the garden as mutated by earlier rules in the same day, so one rule's action (e.g. watering) suppressed or triggered another rule on the same tile depending on rule order. WORKBENCH.md: "Rules respond to the day's growing conditions consistently, even when several care actions are needed." run_rules now snapshots the post-growth conditions once and evaluates every rule against that snapshot.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Tile moisture 20. Rule 1: moisture below 30 → water; rule 2: moisture below 30 → compost, same tile. After step(), only water ran (rule 2 saw moisture 52). After fix both rules act because the day's condition was below 30.

provisional_claims.summary: Save validation accepted duplicate daily history points (same day twice) because the check used `<` rather than `<=`; history is one census per day and the error states "History days must increase". Duplicate days now rejected.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Take a save with workbench.history [{day:1,...}] and append a copy with day 1; World.from_dict accepted it. Now raises ValueError("History days must increase").

provisional_claims.summary: CLI `forecast -o` only compared the raw path strings, so an equivalent spelling of the source path (e.g. `forecast ./g.json -o g.json` or an absolute path) overwrote the source garden with the predicted future. PORTABILITY: "A forecast requires a different output path from its source." Paths are now compared after resolve().
provisional_claims.reproduction: cd dir; python -m mosslight new g.json; python -m mosslight forecast ./g.json --days 2 -o g.json → exit 0 and g.json advanced 2 days. Now exits 2 with "Forecast output must differ from the source garden" and leaves the source unchanged.

provisional_claims.summary: Loaded gardens shared workbench data with the input save: state.validate used a shallow raw.copy(), so World.from_dict(data) aliased data's tiles/notes/plans lists; later garden edits silently mutated the caller's save dict (and validation rewrote note tags in the caller's data). Now the workbench is deep-copied on load.
provisional_claims.reproduction: d=w.to_dict(); w2=World.from_dict(d); w2.workbench['tiles'][0]['mulch']=50; add_note(w2,'y') -> d['workbench']['tiles'][0]['mulch']==50 and d gained the note. After fix d is unchanged.

provisional_claims.summary: World.from_dict kept the caller's journal entry dicts (shallow list copy), so a loaded garden shared journal objects with the input save; editing the source dict (or a to_dict snapshot passed back in) silently changed the live garden's journal. Journal is now deep-copied on load, like the workbench.
provisional_claims.reproduction: d=create().to_dict(); w2=World.from_dict(d); d['journal'][0]['text']='x'; w2.journal[0]['text'] became 'x'. After fix it remains 'A little world wakes beneath the glass.'.

provisional_claims.summary: World.index accepted booleans as coordinates (isinstance(x, int) is true for True/False), so commands like {"op":"tend","args":{"x":true,"y":0,...}} silently acted on tile 1,0 instead of being rejected as non-integer coordinates. Now uses an exact int type check, consistent with validation.integer.
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(34); w.index(True,0) returned 1; execute(w,{"op":"tend","args":{"x":true,"y":0,"action":"water"}}) watered tile (1,0). Now raises 'Coordinates must be integers'.

provisional_claims.summary: Propagation bench: hydrated days only improved vigor for batches still "growing"; watered "ready" batches gained nothing even though WORKBENCH.md says "A batch needs regular watering even after it is ready ... Hydrated days develop the batch and improve its vigor". Hydrated days now add vigor (+3, capped at 100) for any living batch.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Start a clover seed batch (ready after 2 days), keep watering; after it becomes ready its vitality stayed constant on every hydrated day. After fix it increases by 3 per hydrated day up to 100.

provisional_claims.summary: harvest() only reduced plant age by 5, so any plant at least harvest_age+5 days old could be harvested again immediately and repeatedly, contradicting WORKBENCH.md: "Harvesting takes vigor and starts a new growth period before the next harvest" (same pattern as seed collection, which restarts the plant's growth). Harvest now restarts the growth period (age 0), so the species harvest age must elapse again before the next harvest.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Moss age 30 vitality 90 at (0,0): harvest → age 25; harvest again immediately succeeds (age 25 ≥ harvest_age 8) and again... After fix the second harvest raises "Harvest needs age 8 and vitality 40" until 8 more days have grown.
